products.name: 'Resembling Peacock Feathers' Tenmoku Tea Cup
products.description:
These are luxury-grade Tenmoku tea cups handmade by the renowned artist Ding Changsheng (丁长生). Available in two different shapes, they are glazed with a multicolor oil specks pattern resembling peacock feathers on display. The metallic blue glaze color changes depending on how the light illuminates it, with purple, green, and golden nuances enriching the beautiful appearance of these cups. Every piece has a unique pattern, naturally formed during oven firing at 1300ºC.

These high-quality Tenmoku tea cups come with an elegant gift box and a certificate of authenticity, hand-signed by the artist Ding.

products.name: 'Silver Fur' Tenmoku Tea Cup
products.description:
A blue Tenmoku tea cup (also known as 'Jian Zhan') with a naturally formed pattern due to oven-firing at high temperature (1300ºC). This kind of pattern is also known as 'hare's fur' with vertical stripes resembling animal fur.

History
During the Song Dynasty, skilled artisans at the Jian kilns crafted exquisite tea bowls. Due to their humble appearance they were first loved by monks in Buddhist temples. As the wisps of steam twirled above the tea's surface, the divine contrast between the luminous glaze of these bowls and the white foam of whipped tea cast a spell on those who sipped from them.

News of these enchanted bowls quickly spread beyond the monastery walls. When word reached the finest tea connoisseur of them all, Song Emperor Huizong, he declared that the black-glazed bowls decorated with intricate 'hare's fur' patterns were the most desirable of all. Holding the secrets to the powerful art of ritual tea preparation, these remarkable tea bowls soon found their way to Japan during the Kamakura period, with Japanese monks unlocking the mysteries of southern China's Buddhist temples. The Jian Zhan cups, were called 'Tenmoku' in Japan.

products.name: 'Origin of Life' Blue Shu Kou Tenmoku Tea Cup
products.description:
A majestic Tenmoku (or 'Jian Zhan') tea cup with a naturally formed blue pattern due to oven-firing at high temperature (1300ºC). It's made in the most popular shape known as 'bound rim' or 'shu kou' which resembles an inverted cap of a mushroom.
Shu Kou (Bound Rim) Tea Cup Shape

The Shu Kou tea cup features a delicately curved rim, which was originally designed to prevents any spillage when pouring the tea during tea competitions. Due to its relatively deep shape, it's also known as a 'deep tea cup'.

products.name: Mingche 'Dunhuang Lotus Realm' Gilded Jian Ware Zen Meditation Tea Cup
products.description:
In the distant oasis of Dunhuang, sacred lotuses bloom serenely amidst vibrant, storied caisson ceilings. Echoing this ancient beauty, graceful lotus motifs adorn the cup, carrying a timeless Zen resonance that speaks of purification and rebirth. An embossed lotus rests at the base, evoking shadows of blossoms swaying gently across clear waters; in an instant, past and present, stillness and motion, all find harmonious rest within a single pour of tea.

As delicate steam curls upward, the soul finds a peaceful sanctuary amid gentle tea fragrances and shifting floral reflections—quiet, contemplative, and luminous with inner clarity.

Each petal of the Dunhuang Lotus Realm tenderly embraces the next, quietly narrating thousands of years of classic elegance. Crafted from premium ceramic, painstakingly polished, and fired at high temperatures, the cup offers a silky, jade-like touch. The essence of ancient lotus patterns weaves seamlessly with the unpredictable glaze shifts born of the kiln, while fluid silhouettes and dappled textures catch the light in captivating splendor.

With every sip, a mellow sweetness blooms softly on the palate. More than a refined vessel for daily tea rituals, it is an exquisite gift that carries profound affection and respect. Whether presented to esteemed partners or cherished friends, it conveys an authentic cultural discernment that never fades into the ordinary—thoughtfully packaged, with sincerity felt in every detail.
